references.text: The Lord guided his people with faithfulness, a parallel to how he alone led Israel.
The psalmist expresses trust that the Lord alone gives security, reflecting the theme that God alone leads his people.
Describes how God led his people like a flock through the wilderness, paralleling God's solitary leadership of Israel.
The command that there should be no foreign god among them, linked to the fact that no foreign god was with the Lord.
The Lord declares that before him no god was formed and after him none shall come, confirming that he alone is God.
The Lord proclaims that he is the first and the last, and there is no God besides him.
The angel of the Lord saved them, and he carried them all the days of old, paralleling God's solitary leadership.
God taught Ephraim to walk and took them up in his arms, an image of God's personal guidance of his people.
